Native informational response path: source writer -> bounded per-request InformationalSender -> existing H1 driver/encoder/flush acknowledgement or existing H2 stream SendResponse::send_informational. Intermediate headers leave the final response and handler header map uncommitted and uncleared.

HTTP/1 101 remains a final upgrade response; bundled Go HTTP/2 treats its 1xx class separately. HTTP/1 explicit 100 or final headers disable deferred automatic Continue. HTTP/2 body-read Continue remains its separate source state, including source Expect removal and multi-value token rules.

Server-level OPTIONS * bypasses mux dispatch, emits zero Content-Length, drains up to the source 4KB bound and closes an oversized HTTP/1 connection. Unknown HTTP/1 expectations produce the source empty 417 with Connection close before user handlers.

Full ordered 512-byte Go sniff table includes HTML/XML/PDF/PostScript/BOM/images/audio/video/MP4/fonts/archives/WASM/text. Detection uses the first emitted buffered chunk, not the first small handler write.

ResponseWriter now owns source 2048-byte H1 and 4096-byte H2 buffering, direct large writes, header snapshots and no-body/HEAD/header-presence/Content-Encoding/Transfer-Encoding decisions. H1 signed length parsing and H2 deferred unsigned-63-bit parsing retain their distinct count/error and empty-write behavior.

Attempted int64 write count wraps and includes rejected length overruns; failed transport writes retain the original error chain through one shared sticky failure. Header transport failures are ignored as in source WriteHeader, while the native connection retains its failure.

Source clock and default HTTP diagnostic capabilities are statically supplied by UtilityRuntimeProviders. Date is generated only when its header key is absent, with native automatic dates disabled; Go status-line strings and unknown-code fallback are supplied to the existing reason-phrase extension.

Hyper H2 stream/upgrade futures now use a weak executor and the existing per-connection UtilityTaskScope. Normal/error connection exits cancel and join protocol children; emergency scope Drop aborts owned children. No discarded TokioExecutor JoinHandles or competing lifecycle manager.

Trailer declarations now follow source comma/ASCII-space splitting, canonicalization and the exact httpguts forbidden-name table. H1 retains duplicate declarations and prefixed fields; H2 de-duplicates and promotes prefixed fields with unordered canonical-key collision choices.

Actual response trailer I/O: ResponseWriter publishes one source-encoded H1 field block before yielding its trailers frame. The pinned native connection consumes it only for this response's chunked body, independent of client TE or prior Trailer declarations. Source Header.Write sorting, key spelling, CR/LF replacement and trimming are authored. H2 emits actual trailers frames through the existing h2 body sender, including key-presence with empty values.

Bounded response messages now carry end-of-stream decisions. HTTP/2 HEAD and completed empty responses can end on HEADERS, final data can carry END_STREAM, and present trailers end on their HEADERS frame. This is authored source control flow, not a native frame/parity observation.

Source HTTP/2 Connection first-value exactly close removes that field and signals its connection-owned graceful-close token. The existing Hyper connection driver owns shutdown/GOAWAY and independent stream draining; no new server or task manager.

Plain and TLS accept loops share one per-listener AcceptBackoff, 5ms doubling to 1s, reset on success, via static CGP SourceHttpDelay. Error handling checks shutdown before retry and retains permanent native errors. The source syscall-wrapped Unix/Windows Errno policy is distinct from the direct-Errno exception and Winsock lookalikes; native error-origin and display profiles remain open.

One RequestBody owner is shared by HttpRequest and ResponseWriter: actual Incoming data/trailers, bounded pending frame bytes, remaining length, underlying and Continue-reader EOF/closed state, H1 early Close and native H2 close/read wakeup. Source reads, pre-response discard and explicit/deferred cleanup use that same owner; no detached reader or second body manager.

HTTP/1 pre-response discard now retains the 256KB threshold and separate limit+1 read rule. H1 Close uses its distinct strict-greater-than size rule, fixed copy bound, early-close flag and request-closing/chunked branch. OPTIONS reads at most its remaining 4KB limit plus one source byte per call. Body Close is async and the existing FourZeroFour caller awaits it after the successful-read/error-response path.

Source H1 framing decisions now include inferred lengths, HEAD/no-body suppression, identity versus chunked transfer, conflicting Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length handling, HTTP/1.0 keep-alive and close rules, Continue-reader EOF, source full-duplex opt-in, Date/sniff/header-key presence and protocol-switch Connection preservation. The source handler fields and extraHeader fields remain separate output stages; the latter use Date/length/type/connection/transfer order.

SourceResponse carries immutable H1 fields/framing into the existing native role/connection encoder. Normal and informational source fields use Go Header.Write byte normalization, original key spelling and sorted map order. Source chunks use lowercase hex. Source Content-Length mode does not add native truncation, a competing attempted-byte counter, or an early body-end decision; the source writer retains wrapping/rejected-write accounting.

SourceResponseEnd is published once by the existing request phase after handler return and body cleanup, with declared-length/attempted-count, write-failure, close-after-reply and early-body-close decisions. The existing H1 driver waits before reuse, including HEAD/no-body replies, and preserves queued I/O. Emergency request-phase Drop publishes close. No new actor, executor, registry or lifecycle manager.

Connection disposal now cancels its request children through the existing connection phase. Normal H1 response-body disposal no longer cancels a still-running no-body handler; H2 keeps independent stream/body disposal cancellation. Production parent/source-profile and native schedule reconciliation remain open.

Source H1 heads now bypass the native response-metadata keep-alive heuristic, including separately encoded HTTP/1.0 extra fields. Explicit native shutdown is retained and cannot be re-enabled by a source head. Source close-delimited output likewise defers physical close to handler/body-cleanup completion rather than ending that phase at byte EOF.

Headers now retains raw byte names, nil-map identity and shared map descriptors; HeaderValues retains nil versus non-nil empty, an independent length/capacity/offset view and one shared backing owner. Map clone, shallow copy and source deep copy are distinct operations. Indexed writes and in-capacity append retain aliases; growth allocates separate backing. Bundled H2 uses its separate per-key clone and nil-to-non-nil-empty rule. Informational filtering uses a new map without clearing the handler map. Native H1 header serialization still sorts raw keys independently of source map iteration.
